problem_statement: Travilo is a multi-page travel marketing site: a homepage with a destination/date/guest hero search and a Tour Packages carousel (Italy, Brazil, Egypt cards), plus Destinations, Hotels, Tours, Blog and Contact routes, a desktop header nav (Home / Trips / Flight / Blog / Hotel), a Signup CTA and a hidden mobile menu. Travellers can browse destinations and full tour packages, but there is no curated set of short, ready-to-book breaks and no consistent place to jump from 'I have a few days free' to a confirmed itinerary. Add a new cross-page Getaways section that keeps Travilo's design system. Build a getaways.html page from the shared masthead/header, the reusable inner-banner breadcrumb, the popular-block destination card grid, and the site-wide footer, presenting six curated short getaways (each with a location label, an h3 title, a short description, a duration, a starting price, and clear 'View Tour Packages' and 'Talk to an advisor' actions), and mention a 72h advisor handoff. Add a shared 'Trip readiness' four-step strip (Pick a getaway / Check readiness / View Tour Packages / Talk to an advisor) that renders on both the homepage rail and the Getaways page and wraps cleanly on 390px mobile without horizontal overflow. Add a 'Trip readiness' duration selector (Weekend / Short break / Long weekend) whose chips update a live 'Planning window:' readout when clicked. Register 'Getaways' in the shared header navigation so the same nav-link renders cross-page on the homepage and the new Getaways page, without changing the existing hero search, Tour Packages, routes, imagery, footer, or mobile menu.
design_constraints: Reuse Travilo's existing static design system: the auto-container width, the main-header nav, the inner-banner breadcrumb, the popular-block / package-block card grid, the Travilo orange accent, rounded shadowed white cards, theme-btn button styling, and the site-wide main-footer.

Add getaways.html as a NEW page from the shared chrome; do not remove or restyle the homepage hero search, the Tour Packages carousel, or the existing Destinations / Hotels / Tours / Blog / Contact routes.
Register a single 'Getaways' entry in the shared header navigation registry so the nav-link renders cross-page (homepage and the new page), reusing the existing navigation markup and styling.
Ground the getaways in existing Travilo destinations and flows: real local destination imagery, the Tour Packages route, and the Contact advisor handoff.
Keep the site a dependency-free static site served with a plain static server (python http.server or equivalent); no build step, no new dependencies, no remote assets or iframes.
The Getaways page and homepage must read cleanly on desktop and 390px mobile without horizontal overflow.
required_content: A new Getaways page (getaways.html) is reachable and shows a labeled Getaways section built from the shared card grid with six curated short-getaway cards.
Each getaway card uses the shared design system (location label, an h3 title, description, duration, starting price) and offers 'View Tour Packages' and 'Talk to an advisor' actions.
A shared 'Trip readiness' four-step strip renders on both the homepage rail and the Getaways page and wraps without horizontal overflow on 390px mobile.

A 'Trip readiness' duration selector updates a live 'Planning window:' readout to the selected window (Weekend / Short break / Long weekend) when its chips are clicked — for example, clicking the 'Short break' chip updates the readout to read 'Planning window: Short break', and clicking 'Long weekend' makes it read 'Planning window: Long weekend'.
'Getaways' is registered in the shared header navigation as a nav-link that renders on BOTH the homepage and the Getaways page.

The original Travilo hero search, Tour Packages, Italy/Brazil/Egypt cards, header nav, Signup, footer and hidden mobile menu remain intact; the change is source HTML/CSS/JS only with no dependencies, generated screenshots, iframes, or remote assets.
state_constraints: desktop_home, mobile_home and tablet_home capture the original Travilo hero/search shell and header nav, now carrying the registered Getaways nav-link and the Getaways home rail strip.
desktop_getaways, mobile_getaways and tablet_getaways capture the new Getaways page: the shared header/nav, the readiness strip, the getaways card grid, and the site-wide footer.

desktop_getaways_default captures the Getaways page before any interaction; desktop_getaways_short and desktop_getaways_long capture it after clicking the Short break / Long weekend duration chips, with the 'Planning window:' readout updated to match.

change_completion: A Getaways page renders a labeled Getaways section with six curated short-getaway cards.

The section names real getaways (Bosphorus Weekend Escape, Marrakech Medina Getaway, Bali Rice-Terrace Retreat, Venice Canals Short Break, Dubai Desert Long Weekend, Fjord Paddle Adventure) and mentions the 72h advisor handoff.
The duration selector updates the 'Planning window:' readout to the selected window when its chips are clicked.
design_consistency: The Getaways page reuses Travilo's masthead, inner-banner, popular-block card grid, orange accent, rounded shadowed cards, button rhythm and site-wide footer.
The shared 'Trip readiness' strip renders in the same light rounded-tile style on both the homepage rail and the Getaways page, and 'Getaways' is a registered header nav-link on both pages.
regression: Travilo logo, Home/Trips/Flight/Blog/Hotel nav, Signup, hero destination search, Tour Packages, the tour/contact routes and the hidden mobile menu remain available.
The static site still serves with a plain static server and requires no build step or new dependencies.
responsive: desktop_home, mobile_home and tablet_home preserve the original hero/search shell and header nav.
desktop_getaways, mobile_getaways and tablet_getaways show the Getaways section and the readiness strip without clipping or horizontal overflow on tablet and 390px mobile.

author_notes: Slot slot_239 (product-grade L4) targets MdShahriarFerdous/TravelWebsite-HTML-Template, an unused runnable static Travilo travel marketing site.
